summary: Scott County, TN tower the Tennessee Landforms table calls Brimstone 16 and marks removed; OpenStreetMap names it Lookout Tower Number Sixteen and gives a conflicting elevation.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed in the Tennessee Landforms tower table; no source we read describes what remains on the site.

evidence.supports: named Brimstone 16 in the Tennessee Landforms table
OpenStreetMap point named Lookout Tower Number Sixteen
state waypoint Brimstone 16 at 36.2835, -84.4678, about 66 m from the OpenStreetMap point
waypoint elevation 888.2 meters, which is 2,914 feet

notes_for_editor: Name conflict: the Tennessee Landforms table says Brimstone 16, OpenStreetMap says Lookout Tower Number Sixteen (already in the record's other_names). Elevation conflict: 2,914 ft in the table (its waypoint file gives 888.2 m) against 879 m on OpenStreetMap; the metric conversion in the story is ours (2,914 ft is about 888 m). Location check: the OpenStreetMap node (36.283394, -84.468526) is about 66 m from the Brimstone 16 waypoint (36.2835, -84.4678) in towers.gpx, so the story treats the two as one tower. The tower is not on the NHLR Tennessee list by name and is not named in the NPS forestry-towers form. Searches found no history. A June 2026 fire on Brimstone Road in Scott County appeared in search results; no source ties it to the tower, so it is left out.
